title: Dirac or Majorana — nothing makes a Majorana mass, nothing forbids one
plain: A neutrino could be its own antiparticle if the theory contained one specific extra term. On the current stack that term is exactly zero, so neutrinos come out Dirac by default. Nobody has shown that no admissible extension could switch it on. Until that is decided, the seesaw mechanism, Majorana phases and the neutrinoless-double-beta rate are unavailable, and the answer is left to experiment.

title: Absolute mass scale — the two routes to tiny masses cannot both be reached from the stack
plain: There are two standard ways to make neutrinos very light: give each a very heavy partner (seesaw), or use an unexplained tiny coupling. The stack switches the first off (W1). Using its own coupling directly gives a neutrino mass about 1 GeV, some twenty billion times too big. The repo's one numerical success uses the seesaw, so it sits on a surface the stack calls empty.

title: The one quantitative success stands on posited bridges
plain: The lane hits one measured number, the atmospheric mass gap, within a few percent. Getting there needs choices the axioms do not fix: two "minimal lift" rules placing the heavy partners on a ladder, a rule for splitting them, a coupling formula that includes a measured coupling, and a weak-scale value from another lane. The staircase notes behind it have never been audited. A ladder this coarse lands this close by luck roughly once in 70 to 200 tries.

title: The mass pattern beyond the atmospheric gap is wrong or absent
plain: Apart from the one good number, the benchmark has the wrong shape: one light state and two nearly equal heavy ones. The "solar" gap comes out about 28 times too large, and the total mass (0.10 eV) exceeds a limit the repo itself quotes. The mixing chart cannot help: its mass-like numbers have a ratio ten times off. No law yet fixes neutrino mass ratios.

title: Mixing angles — the stack gives none, and the extension that gives them is set by the data
plain: The theory's own tools give no neutrino mixing. Large mixing appears only after adding an extra piece with three free knobs, and those knobs are set from the measured angles. One proposed rule (three simple equations) sets the knobs so all three angles sit within 1σ of data, but two of its equations are unproved. So the three angles are inputs, not results.

title: CP phase and octant — the only live prediction rests on a one-bit sheet choice and leans against current data
plain: The lane's sharp forecast is a CP-violation phase near −90° with the atmospheric angle above 45°. The phase's sign is a one-bit choice the theory cannot make: flipping one constant mirrors it exactly. The quoted range was built when data favoured it. The repo's own NuFIT-6.1 comparison puts the current best fit outside the range and the angle below 45°. DUNE and Hyper-K will decide.

title: Three routes to the mixing cannot all be true
plain: The repo tells three different stories about the mixing. The chart fits the measured angles. The records story says the middle neutrino is exactly an equal mix of all three flavours, which pushes θ12 outside the current 3σ range unless another unexplained rotation is added. The mass benchmark instead makes the equal-mix state the lightest. On the same operator they give incompatible answers.

title: The objects the lane computes on are not supplied by the four axioms, and nothing in the lane is audited
plain: Every neutrino result assumes objects the axioms do not contain: chiral fermions, a neutral right-handed neutrino, three generations, Higgs doublets and gauge couplings. The neutrino's neutrality is a labelling convention. The fermion realization is a listed open gate. All 326 neutrino/PMNS rows in the audit ledger are unaudited, and none of 131 lane notes cites the current axiom memo.
